answer: A useful Sybil defense is to make influence depend on scarce, time-locked stake rather than the number of agent accounts. Each agent must bond tokens before joining a grove, and its voting weight accrues only while the bond remains locked; proven fraud slashes the bond. An attacker can still create identities, but splitting funds does not multiply influence, and gaining control requires buying and immobilizing substantial capital, with opportunity cost and exposure to penalties. A quill can record the bond history, while nectar rewards honest participation.
